title: Structure and dynamics in solution of the stop codon decoding N-terminal domain of the human polypeptide chain release factor eRF1.
experiment: 15N longitudinal (R1) and transverse (R2) relaxation and 15N{1H} heteronuclear NOE at 600 MHz (14 T) with Clore extended Lipari-Szabo model-free analysis (RelaxFit)
buffer: 10 mM sodium phosphate, 25 mM NaCl, ~2 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, 90% H2O/10% D2O
construct_or_mutation: human eRF1 N-terminal domain (N-eRF1, residues 1-142) with C-terminal His6-tag
other_conditions: protein concentration: ~1 mM [U-15N] N-eRF1; tumbling: 1/(2D_parallel + 4D_perp) = 11.04 ± 0.16 ns, D_parallel/D_perp = 1.6 ± 0.1 (axially symmetric rotational diffusion tensor); S2_slow between 0.3 and 1.0, S2_fast = 0.9 ± 0.1 (between 0.8 and 1.0 in Fig. S5) (supp_PMC3403424_pro0021-0896-SD1.pdf); 仅图示: per-residue R1, R2, NOE, S2, and Rex plotted in Fig. 2A and Supporting Information Figs. S4 and S6A
timescale: tau_slow = 1.05 ± 0.05 ns (between 1 and 1.1 ns in Fig. S5); tau_fast < 50 ps (between 0 and 50 ps in supplement) (two-time-scale extended Lipari-Szabo model-free fit with axially symmetric diffusion tensor in RelaxFit; ms-timescale Rex fitted per residue and plotted in Fig. S4)
related_structures: 2LLX (solution NMR structure ensemble of human eRF1 N-domain, 20 conformers, this work)
author_claim: 15N R1, R2, and 15N{1H} NOE relaxation and two-time-scale extended model-free analysis at 600 MHz (298 K) identify fast (<50 ps) and ~1 ns (1.05 ± 0.05 ns) internal motions with lowest order parameters S2 at the N- and C-termini and loops 30-33 (GTS stop-codon decoding loop), 64 (NIKS loop), 106-108, and 122-123 (specifically 30-31, 64, and 122-123 at ~1 ns), alongside ms-timescale conformational exchange (Rex) at residues 45, 54-57, 63, 67, and 134-135 in helices alpha2-alpha3 and adjacent loops.
anchor: correlation time of fast motion between 0 and 50 ps; correlation time of slow motion τslow 1.05 ± 0.05 ns; order parameter of fast motions S2fast 0.9 ± 0.1.
locator: supp_PMC3403424_pro0021-0896-SD1.pdf, NMR dynamics analysis and Figs. S4-S6 (仅图示); main text Results (Backbone dynamics), Discussion, Fig. 2A (仅图示), and Materials and Methods
caveat_note: Matches BMRB 18092 (explicitly cited as BMRB-18092, depositing chemical shifts and R1, R2, and 15N{1H} NOE values at 298 K, pH 6.8, 600 MHz, 1 mM NeRF1, 10 mM sodium phosphate, 25 mM NaCl, 2 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, 90% H2O/10% D2O; BMRB S1-S5 additionally list 0.01% sodium azide). Manifest card lists uniprot P03355, whereas text studies Homo sapiens eRF1 N-domain (residues 1-142). Per-residue Rex (s-1) and S2 values are plotted only in Fig. 2A and Supporting Information Figs. S4 and S6A rather than tabulated in text. Results lists smallest S2 in loops (30-33, 64, 106-108, 122-123), whereas Discussion highlights 30-31, 64, and 122-123 for ~1 ns motions. Main text PDF prints '6' for '±' due to font encoding (11.04 6 0.16 ns, 1.05 6 0.05 ns), verified as '±' in supplement.

title: Structure and dynamics in solution of the stop codon decoding N-terminal domain of the human polypeptide chain release factor eRF1.
experiment: 15N-1H HSQC and 3D heteronuclear/NOESY slow-exchange peak doubling analysis at 600 and 800 MHz
buffer: 10 mM sodium phosphate, 25 mM NaCl, ~2 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, 90% H2O/10% D2O (or 100% D2O)
construct_or_mutation: human eRF1 N-terminal domain (N-eRF1, residues 1-142) with C-terminal His6-tag
other_conditions: protein concentration: ~1 mM; regime (authors): slow exchange producing duplicate sets of signals (double peaks) for backbone and side-chain amides; 仅图示: additional peak-doubled residues at the beta-sheet core / helices alpha2-alpha3 interface shown in Fig. 2B (blue side chains) and Supporting Information Fig. S1 (red peaks)
related_structures: 2LLX (solution NMR structure ensemble of human eRF1 N-domain, 20 conformers, this work)
author_claim: Several backbone and side-chain amides of human eRF1 N-domain exhibit duplicate sets of NMR signals with a ~5:1 intensity ratio representing major (80-90%) and minor (10-20%) conformational states; large chemical shift differences (including the N111 side chain and residues at the beta-sheet/alpha2-alpha3 interface) indicate reorientation of helices alpha2 and alpha3 and the NIKS loop relative to the beta-core.
anchor: Side chains of residues which have large chemical shift differences between the major and minor conformers are shown in blue.
locator: Fig. 2B (仅图示); Results (Resonance assignment; Minor protein conformer); Discussion; supp_PMC3403424_pro0021-0896-SD1.pdf Fig. S1 (仅图示); conditions: Materials and Methods
caveat_note: Only Asn111 (N111) is named in text among the residues with duplicated peaks; the remaining double-peak residues are shown only graphically in Fig. 2B and Supporting Information Fig. S1. No interconversion rate constant (kex) between major and minor conformers is reported. Materials and Methods states 'The best 20 structures out of 50 ... were accepted as the final ensemble for each protein conformer', but only one PDB accession (2LLX) and one Table I ensemble are reported.

title: Structure and dynamics in solution of the stop codon decoding N-terminal domain of the human polypeptide chain release factor eRF1.
experiment: Backbone superposition and local RMSD (qi) comparison of solution NMR ensemble (2LLX) against full-length human eRF1 X-ray crystal structure (Ref. 8)
buffer: 10 mM sodium phosphate, 25 mM NaCl, ~2 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, 90% H2O/10% D2O or 100% D2O (plus ~5% v/w C12E5/hexanol for RDC sample)
construct_or_mutation: isolated human eRF1 N-domain (residues 1-142, His6-tag; 2LLX) vs N-domain in full-length human eRF1 crystal structure (Ref. 8)
other_conditions: global backbone heavy-atom (Calpha, N, O, C') RMSD between 20 NMR structures (residues 6-142) and crystal structure = 1.8 ± 0.1 Å (intra-ensemble NMR backbone RMSD = 0.510 ± 0.087 Å); local RMSD plotted in Fig. 1C and Supporting Information Fig. S6B
related_structures: 2LLX (solution NMR structure ensemble of human eRF1 N-domain, this work); human eRF1 crystal structure cited as Ref. 8 (Song et al. 2000, PDB code not printed in paper)
author_claim: Superposition of the solution NMR ensemble of isolated N-eRF1 (2LLX) onto the crystal structure of full-length human eRF1 (backbone RMSD 1.8 ± 0.1 Å) reveals substantial local backbone divergence in loops 29-33 (GTS), 61-64 (NIKS), and 101-105 that are distant from the M- and C-domains and coincide with dynamic loops, whereas divergence in loop 115-123 and the C-terminus (and secondary changes at 41-42 and 89-91) likely originates from absence of the M- and C-domains in the isolated NMR construct.
anchor: The thickness of the ribbon is proportional to the RMSD values for the heavy atoms of each residue i after superposition of the family of 20 NMR structures onto the crystal structure
locator: Fig. 1; Results, Comparison of the crystal and solution structures; Discussion; supp_PMC3403424_pro0021-0896-SD1.pdf Fig. S6B; conditions: Materials and Methods
caveat_note: The PDB ID of the reference human eRF1 crystal structure (Ref. 8, Song et al. 2000) is not printed in paper.txt, so alt_state_structure is 'none assigned'. Authors note that loop 115-123 and C-terminal differences (plus secondary effects at 41-42 and 89-91) likely reflect truncation of the neighboring M- and C-domains rather than intrinsic solution-vs-solid switching, whereas loops 29-33, 61-64, and 101-105 are distant from interdomain contacts.
